terra.problem: Saying Paul did not take even a quick cookie break adds an unsupported detail about his journey.
The text does not say Paul declared everything helpful at each individual house.
Paul's love for the elders is stated as a fact rather than marked as Papa Dorin's inference.
Saying safety is not Paul's plan goes beyond the text. He says he does not know what will happen to him.
Paul says the men will distort the truth to draw disciples after them. The explanation states that they succeed in taking followers with them.
Paul says his hands provided for his needs and his companions' needs. The passage does not say he never relied on the church.
Saying nobody was being brave adds an unsupported judgment about the elders. Weeping openly does not establish a lack of bravery.
The text says the elders accompanied Paul to the ship, not that they went as far as they could.
The passage does not establish that Jerusalem was not the elders' destination. It only says they accompanied Paul to the ship.
